SQLite SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER defaults to 999; sessions with 999+ findings are unrealistic in practice. The chunking overhead is not justified.

N+1 query on waived/accepted_risk findings: these are typically single-digit count per session. The performance impact is negligible for SQLite local DB access.
cell_start emitted before executor.submit is a design choice for progress reporting. The events are informational; the batched submission pattern is intentional for the ThreadPoolExecutor usage.
stdout/stderr interleaving by index is a best-effort tail display. There is no timestamp information available from subprocess.PIPE output. The round-robin approach is an acceptable approximation.

Defense-in-depth: the redundant is_relative_to check in merge_session_worktree is intentional. If merge_preflight_blockers is ever refactored or called conditionally, this guard still protects the critical path.
Idempotent cleanup by design: when the worktree directory is already absent, treating it as removed allows cleanup to proceed to branch deletion. This is intentional behavior, not a bug.

TOCTOU race is theoretical: review-gauntlet sessions are single-process CLI operations. Concurrent session creation for the same session_id does not occur in practice. git worktree add -b failure would surface a clear error.
The git helper operates on a small review-gauntlet worktree with a handful of files and no pre-commit hooks. The 10-second default is sufficient for this use case.

Executor is created at line 1230, try block starts at 1233, but no exception can occur between those lines (dict literal and bool assignment). The finally block at 1260 always shuts down the executor. No leak exists.

The broad ValueError catch at line 550 is intentional — it converts user-facing validation errors (invalid session ID, bad path, etc.) into clean CLI failures. Internal programming errors would raise different exception types (TypeError, AttributeError, etc.).

The reason parameter is written to a SQLite TEXT column. Practically, review-gauntlet sessions are agent-driven with controlled inputs. Adding a length limit would be an over-constraint for the current usage pattern.
str(row) or None pattern is fragile — if COALESCE is removed and value is SQL NULL, str(None) produces 'None' (truthy string). Should use explicit conditional.
